checks.finding: The requirements give measurable outcomes and validation rules, including exact Phase 1/2 tuples (REQ-001, REQ-008), ownership checks (REQ-003), and rollback branches (REQ-009); an implementer or verifier can determine whether each is satisfied.
Each stated goal REQ-001–REQ-014 has at least one mapped acceptance criterion in requirements.md; the acceptance table also maps each criterion to a planned TEST-ID.

REQ-004 requires overrides to appear only on component or approved cross-cutting records and requires each entry to have exactly four fields, rejecting missing or extra fields (requirements.md:135-146). AC-030/031 assert the two valid entries and test unknown names, out-of-scope entries, and no-op values, but do not specify an observable rejection for malformed field sets or placement on another record type (acceptance-tests.md:36-37). A verifier could accept those nonconforming cases under the listed oracles; this is a Phase 1 acceptance-coverage gap.
The non-goals explicitly exclude later Packs, architecture replacements, UI/cloud deployment, new CI workflows, and approval of specs, tasks, sidecars, or WFIs (requirements.md:333-339).

Material approval, security, dependency, compatibility, and shared-state constraints are stated, including protected publication and human approval (REQ-001, REQ-008), rollback governance (REQ-009), and re-verification of mutable A1–A8 and shared state (REQ-011).

High-risk promotion and rollback claims have planned validation surfaces: promotion evidence and stale/unmet-threshold rejection (AC-012–013), atomic-transition and missing-evidence cases (AC-014–015, AC-033), and rollback security and changed-registry cases (AC-016–018, AC-034).
Skipped: the project root has no domain/ directory, meeting the check's explicit skip condition.
